title: Acceptance criteria: envelope-based emit protocol & tool invocation safety
creator: Priya Shah
description: Define acceptance criteria for a new envelope-based emit protocol that guarantees parsable partial output, explicit tool-invocation boundaries, and safe fallback semantics across streaming and non-streaming modes. This ticket clarifies behavioral expectations for SDKs and server runtimes, cross-service telemetry, and failure handling so engineering can implement a compatible runtime and PM can sign off on regressions and partner contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format: Each top-level emission in streamed and non-streamed responses must be wrapped in a single-line JSON envelope with keys: 'envelope_id', 'type' (one of 'content', 'tool_call', 'checkpoint', 'end'), 'seq' (monotonic per-response), and 'payload' (opaque JSON object). Parsers must ignore unknown top-level keys.

Partial emissions: Consumers can safely parse and recover partial 'content' envelopes even when the stream is truncated; runtime emits a 'checkpoint' envelope every N tokens (configurable; default 512) containing last-valid-parse-offset and schema-hash.

Tool call handshake: A 'tool_call' envelope must include 'tool_name', 'request_id', 'args_schema_version', and an idempotency token. SDKs must surface a deterministic callback API that passes through 'request_id' and 'idempotency_token' to downstream tool adapters.

Fallback policy: If a tool invocation fails synchronously (adapter returns error) or times out, the runtime must emit a 'tool_error' sentinel envelope followed by a 'content' envelope explaining the fallback behavior. Acceptance requires both human-readable fallback and machine-readable error_code.

Streaming/non-streaming parity: Non-streamed responses must preserve envelope ordering and include the same checkpoint and end envelopes so clients using either mode can rely on the same state machine semantics.

Schema negotiation: On first tool_call envelope the runtime must include 'args_schema_version' and a stable 'schema_id'. Client and tool adapters must be able to reject mismatched schema versions; rejection must produce a documented 'schema_mismatch' error envelope and an operator-facing alert in the console.

Idempotency guarantees: Replayed tool_call envelopes with identical idempotency token must be handled idempotently by tool adapters; runtime should retry at most 2 times automatically and surface retry_count in telemetry.

Error classification: Implement three canonical error classes emitted as 'error_class' in error envelopes: 'transient' (retryable), 'permanent' (client/authoring error), and 'adaptor' (third-party/tool adapter failure). Each error envelope must include 'error_code' and optional 'suggested_action'.

Compatibility: New envelope mode must be opt-in via API parameter 'envelope_mode=true' and default to backwards-compatible text output for any client that does not opt in. Acceptance requires no disruption to existing customers when envelope_mode is disabled.

Observability: For every tool_call the platform must emit telemetry events with fields: model, route_id, envelope_mode, tool_name, request_id, idempotency_token, time_to_tool_response_ms, adapter_error_class, and retry_count. Acceptance requires dashboards for 'tool latency' and 'tool error rate' with 7d retention in staging.

Test coverage: Unit tests for envelope encoding/decoding, integration test that simulates mid-stream truncation and verifies checkpoint recovery, and end-to-end test with a mock tool adapter demonstrating idempotent retries and fallback envelopes. Acceptance requires tests in CI and a stable test harness in repo 'infra/streaming-emits/tests'.

Rollout gating: Feature must be behind a runtime flag and staged to <10% traffic in prod with canary dashboards showing error-class rates; acceptance requires no increase >0.5% in 5xx errors and no client-reported schema parse failures during the canary window.
decisions: Use single-line JSON envelopes to simplify streaming parsers and avoid multi-line boundary ambiguity.
Emit periodic 'checkpoint' envelopes rather than every token to balance parseability and token cost; default interval set to 512 tokens.
Make envelope_mode opt-in to preserve backward compatibility for existing SDKs and customers.
Require an idempotency token for tool_call envelopes and limit automatic runtime retries to 2.
Classify errors into three buckets to simplify downstream alerting and automated remediation policies.

notes: Implementation should reuse existing streaming codec where possible; add an envelope wrapper at the transport boundary to avoid touching model output code paths.
Consider a compatibility shim in SDKs that can convert older outputs into envelopes for downstream tools during migration.
Plan pre-flight migration doc for strategic customers who use raw token streaming and cannot opt-in immediately.
Security team to validate that idempotency tokens do not leak PII and are stored encrypted in telemetry pipelines.
